title: Cohomology commutes with direct sums of modules on a qcqs scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in I}$ be any family of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$ be their direct sum, i.e. a coproduct in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with inclusions $\iota_i:\mathcal F_i\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$, and let $p\ge0$. The canonical $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}H^p(X,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(X,\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)$ from the direct sum of modules [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], whose restriction to the $i$-th summand is $H^p(X,\iota_i)$, is an isomorphism [pqf-def-cohomology]. In particular this holds for the family indexed by the nonnegative graded pieces of a quasi-coherent graded module.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01FF (lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit, lines 3194-3225), applied to the directed system of finite partial direct sums; its topological hypotheses hold for the underlying space of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. The finite sums commute with cohomology by additivity. Tag verified in tags/tags: 01FF,cohomology-lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit.

proof.text: Obtain additivity of H^p(X,-) by unfolding the right-derived definition in [pqf-def-cohomology] and applying the upstream instance in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived. This uses the additive global sections functor and additivity of injectiveResolutions, with no cohomological delta-functor theorem.

For each i define pi_i:S to F_i by coproduct descent, taking the identity on summand i and zero on every other summand. Functoriality and preservation of zero identify H^p(pi_i) composed with the canonical direct-sum map with DirectSum.component at i. Extensionality of finite-support functions gives injectivity. This argument does not use compactness or a zero-at-a-later-stage criterion.

For a target class x, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-finite-subsum-representatives] gives a finite J and y in H^p(X,B_J) mapping to x. For each j project y by H^p(biproduct.pi_j), and take the finite sum of DirectSum.lof_j of these projected classes.

Additivity and the finite biproduct identity sum_j pi_j followed by inclusion_j = identity imply sum_j H^p(pi_j) followed by H^p(iota_j) = H^p(kappa_J). Applying this to y shows the finite-support element maps to x. This proves surjectivity. Combine with injectivity to prove bijectivity. The empty finite stage is covered by the same total identity.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01FF and 09J7, with existence of finite-stage representatives split off. Injectivity is proved directly by coproduct projections; surjectivity is constructed using the finite biproduct total identity. Lean reduction written by K1. Second reading: additivity uses the upstream rightDerived additive instance directly.
